source: Agriculture Sector Development Project (ASDP), ADB Loan No. 2023-CAM(SF), Guide No.1: Coconut-damaging beetle and protective measures, prepared by Kampot Province Department of Agricultural Extension, 2008
text:
Since around the year 2000, agricultural staff have observed an increasing outbreak of a coconut-damaging beetle in Cambodia. Symptoms include reddish-brown, scorched-looking discoloration of the young unopened leaves at the crown, dried-out and shortened new leaflets, and stunted growth of newly emerging fronds, since the beetle attacks the tender, still-folded young leaf before it opens.

When the growing point (bud) at the top of the palm is severely and repeatedly attacked, the tree's productivity drops sharply and, in severe cases, the palm can die. The guide notes that this damage has caused economic loss to both national coconut production and to individual farmers' income, and urges farmers and extension workers to recognize the early symptoms (browning of new fronds, stunted leaflets at the crown) so control measures can be applied promptly.
